focus: Data engineering, Python data tools, data quality, pipeline investigation, and practical AI workflow automation
summary: Muzammil Qazi is a Pune-based data engineering and AI workflow automation professional. His public portfolio includes five independent Python applications for pipeline simulation, CSV quality checks, reconciliation, runbook retrieval, and privacy policy experiments.
scope: The five public applications are independent portfolio projects developed with Codex assistance. They use synthetic demonstrations and do not establish employer deployment, client outcomes, certifications, or production adoption.

pipeline-pulse.technical: Discrete-event DAG scheduling; dependency validation; bounded retries; critical-path lower bound; worker-capacity comparisons; Python-graded incident scenarios.
pipeline-pulse.limitation: A deterministic synthetic simulator. It does not connect to Azure or operate a production pipeline.

datalens.category: CSV data quality and distribution drift
datalens.technical: Not-null, uniqueness, numeric, range, and allowed-value contracts; record-level violations; smoothed Population Stability Index comparisons.
datalens.limitation: Contract scores are rule pass rates, not dataset accuracy. PSI thresholds are review heuristics, especially with small samples.

recon-lab.technical: Unique composite-key matching, Decimal arithmetic, absolute and source-relative tolerance, opt-in text normalization, control totals, and exception exports.
recon-lab.limitation: No automatic data repair. Equal totals do not establish record equality; business keys and tolerance policies must be chosen deliberately.

runbook-radar.technical: BM25 and TF-IDF cosine retrieval; adjustable word chunks and overlap; term-level contributions; source passages; labeled mean reciprocal rank and Hit@K evaluation.
runbook-radar.limitation: Lexical retrieval, not a generative LLM assistant. Similarity scores are not confidence probabilities and synthetic evaluations are not production benchmarks.

privacy-forge.technical: Column policies for keeping, dropping, redacting, tokenizing, or generalizing cells; heuristic signals; exact quasi-identifier groups; hashed audit receipts.
privacy-forge.limitation: Heuristic discovery and group-size analysis do not guarantee anonymization. Generalized values can still reveal identifying information.
